Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

Unbuffered streams directly access the disk which makes them slower for large files.

This file is created to compare buffered and unbuffered file copy execution time using System.nanoTime().
Practicing file handling improves understanding of streams, exceptions, and performance optimization in Java.
Java InputStream and OutputStream are used to read and write binary data efficiently.
System.nanoTime is used to measure precise execution time for performance comparison.
Reading and writing in chunks of 4096 bytes improves efficiency compared to byte-by-byte operations.
BufferedInputStream wraps FileInputStream to add an internal memory buffer for faster access.
BufferedOutputStream wraps FileOutputStream to reduce the number of physical disk write operations.
This test file contains repeated data to simulate a large file of several megabytes.
